"""Why does the ridge predictor extrapolate better than the logistic ones? Bias of model-based estimators against the target's distance above the sources.

usage: python3 -I scripts/11_extrap_bias.py results/raw/target_level.parquet results/extrap_bias.csv [split=extrap] [n=100]

For each non-thin benchmark, design and model-based estimator in the extrapolation split: the targets are the top 25 % of models, so gap = true_score - min(true_score)
over the targets of the benchmark measures how far above the sources a target lies (0 = just above the best source, up to the best model). Columns: slope =
least-squares slope of the signed (draw-mean) bias on gap, pooled over benchmarks after dividing both by the benchmark's standard deviation of true_score over targets
(a slope of -1: the estimate falls one target-sd short per target-sd of gap); bias_top = mean bias of the top quarter of targets by gap, in units of that sd;
share_bias2 = bias^2 / (bias^2 + draw variance) pooled.
"""
import sys, numpy as np, pandas as pd

t = d.drop_duplicates(["bench", "target_model"])[["bench", "target_model", "true_score"]]
t = t.assign(sd=t.groupby("bench").true_score.transform("std"), gap=t.true_score - t.groupby("bench").true_score.transform("min"))
